sentence: This project tests how risk proteins linked to Alzheimer's disease and its neuropsychiatric symptoms work in cortical organoids.
This project builds a Magnetic Resonance Imaging method with deep learning to measure how cerebrospinal fluid moves in the human brain.
This project builds technologies to observe, describe and measure the human virome, a large group of viruses that live in the body.
This project uses deep learning with clinical, pathologic, and immune features to predict breast cancer recurrence and chemotherapy benefit.
This project tests whether restoring cellular energy metabolism can reduce HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders and fentanyl dependence, using human organoid models and a rat model.
This project tries to find out the genetic origins of evolutionary novelties and how organs arise during animal evolution.
This project studies how immune cell circuits work in colon cancer and its metastases to lymph nodes and liver, using patient tissue.
This project provides methods and analysis tools for research on social and behavioral processes behind health problems in older adults.
This project studies how rewired signaling in melanoma affects metastasis and resistance, including during aging.
This project updates the Integrative Genomics Viewer, a tool for visualizing genomic data, to keep pace with genomics technology and user needs.
This project studies how androgens and obesity affect blood pressure and insulin resistance in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
This project uses ethnic-specific models to identify women at high risk of breast cancer.
This project studies how a protein linking insulin signaling and glucose uptake affects cardiomyocyte metabolism and the heart's response to metabolic stress.
This project uses genomewide approaches and single-cell transcriptomics to study motor neuron degeneration and find treatment targets in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project studies how after school care for teenagers can reduce the long-term burden of heart disease during pregnancy.
This project studies how temperature controls the gating of certain ion channels and how drugs affect them, using electrophysiological recording.
This project studies digestive disease and the role of host-environment interactions in it.
This project supports HIV research from basic to clinical and behavioral work, with the goal of ending the HIV epidemic.
This project tests how audio-visual features in influencer e-cigarette posts on social media affect how adolescents see e-cigarettes and whether they use them.
This project provides administrative support for cancer research, including management of resources and scientific meetings.
